stepExplanation: In any bacterial population, there is natural genetic variation due to random mutations. Some bacteria, by chance, already possess mutations that confer antibiotic resistance BEFORE exposure to the antibiotic. The antibiotic does not cause the mutation - it acts as a selection pressure that favors bacteria that already have the resistance gene. This is a key principle of natural selection: variation exists first, then selection acts on it.
